title: Noise contraction of the Bobkov functional
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$, and let $0\le\rho\le1$. Then the Bobkov functional of the Boolean noise operator applied to $f$ satisfies $B(T_\rho f)\le B(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the n-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: For a real function $f$ on the uniform Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$, write $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$ and $B(f)=\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_i(D_i f)^2}$, where $\overline I$ is the Gaussian profile extended by zero outside $(0,1)$. For $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,1]$ and $0\le\rho\le1$, $B(T_\rho f)\le B(f)$, where $T_\rho$ is the Boolean noise operator with correlation $\rho$.
